etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin ambiguus (“moving from side to side, of doubtful nature”), from ambigere (“to go about, wander, doubt”), from ambi- (“around, about, on both sides”) + agere (“to drive, move”).

definitions.definition: (obsolete, of a person) Hesitant; uncertain; not taking sides.

quote.citation: 1662, Thomas Salusbury, (Please provide the book title or journal name):
quote.text: And forasmuch as in this same question I am ambiguous, and Simplicius is resolute....
